title: GeoTransolver: Learning Physics on Irregular Domains using Multi-scale Geometry Aware Physics Attention Transformer
claim: A persistent shared context, built once from geometry and global inputs, is injected into every block via cross-attention to anchor computation.
layout: 3 panels, zoom-in expansions left and right of central stack; dashed and dotted connectors
description: A three-part block diagram of the model architecture. The center is a vertical stack. Input Points feed an Encoder, then a series of GALE Blocks separated by a dotted ellipsis, then a Decoder, then the output F(x). Global Properties and Geometry feed a Context Projector at the top. A solid line runs down from the projector and branches into every GALE Block, labeled with tensor shapes [B,H,S,D]. Dashed lines link the input points to the projector. On the left, a peach panel zooms into one GALE Block: LayerNorm, Linear, Slice, State Self Attention, Context Cross Attention (with a pink Context input), Deslice, residual adds, and an MLP. On the right, a purple panel zooms into the Context Projector. It has a multi-scale feature extractor and two tokenizers, which produce tokens that are concatenated into the Context. Pastel green, blue, yellow and pink nodes mark inputs, tensors and modules.
caption: GeoTransolver architecture. Right: the context projector constructs a shared geometry and global context by projecting multi-scale ball-query features and global parameters into slice-token space via a half-attention operation; learned geometric features are also concatenated onto local input tokens. Center: The learned context is continually injected to the model to provide persistent geometrical recall. Left: each GALE block extends Transolver's Physics Attention with the addition of cross attention to the shared global context.
abstract: We present GeoTransolver, a multiscale geometry-aware physics attention transformer for Computer Aided Engineering (CAE). GeoTransolver extends the Transolver backbone with GALE (Geometry-Aware Latent Embeddings) attention, which pairs physics-aware self-attention on learned state slices with cross-attention to a shared geometry and global context computed via multi-scale ball queries (inspired by Domino) and reused in every block. Implemented and released in NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo, GeoTransolver persistently projects geometry and global parameters, into physical state spaces to anchor computations to domain structure and operating regimes. We benchmark on DrivAerML, SHIFT-SUV, and SHIFT-Wing against Domino, Transolver (PhysicsNeMo implementation), and literature-reported AB-UPT, evaluating drag/lift R2 and relative L1 errors on field variables. As an additional nonlinear structural mechanics application, we also report Transolver and GeoTransolver results on bumper-beam and full-vehicle Body-in-White (BIW) crash-dynamics benchmarks, evaluating relative L2 trajectory error and probe-level kinematic MSE. GeoTransolver delivers improved accuracy, robustness to geometry and regime shifts, and favorable data efficiency; we include DrivAerML ablations and qualitative contour and design-trend results, advancing operator learning for high-fidelity surrogates on complex, irregular, non-linear domains.
